messages.subject: Choosing between hcov models
parts:
Hello, 

I have some questions on how to make an informed decision about selecting finite mixture models vs. hybrid mixture models. We fit a series of SECR models on black bears with sex ID's. We fit one set of models with hcov = "sex" and another set with without hcov (some of which included regular heterogeneity and some of which included session, labelled as 'yr'). I have included screenshots of tables with the models, their AIC values, and density estimates. 

As I understand it, the AIC values of models with hcov cannot be compared to other models. As can be seen in the table, though, the models which include latent classes produce significantly different estimates for density. I am not sure why the estimates would be so different, and I was wondering if there is guidance about whether hybrid or finite mixture models are better suited to certain kinds of studies. 

Any help would be greatly appreciated. Thank you so much for your time. 

All the best, 
Elizabeth

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Choosing between hcov models
parts:
Hi
I can't say exactly why the estimates are so different, but it is not too surprising: the 'hcov' approach deals only with heterogeneity due to sex, whereas the finite mixture model (h2) adapts to unmodelled heterogeneity from any source (including e.g. age). I was a bit suspicious that the top h2 model had twice the density of the next model, but that is probably coincidental.

You can directly compare a finite mixture model and a sex-effect model when CL = FALSE. Thus, using built-in data

library(secr)
msk <- make.mask(traps(ovenCHp[[1]]), buffer=250, nx=20)
fithcov  <- secr.fit(ovenCHp[[1]], mask = msk, model=g0~h2, hcov='Sex', trace=F)
fitCLsex <- secr.fit(ovenCHp[[1]], mask = msk, model=g0~Sex, trace=F, CL = TRUE)
fitCLh2  <- secr.fit(ovenCHp[[1]], mask = msk, model=g0~h2, trace=F, CL = TRUE)

# direct comparison OK:
AIC(fitCLsex, fitCLh2)
#                          model   detectfn npar    logLik     AIC    AICc dAICc AICcwt
# fitCLsex        g0~Sex sigma~1 halfnormal    3 -108.9106 223.821 225.321 0.000 0.7611
# fitCLh2  g0~h2 sigma~1 pmix~h2 halfnormal    4 -108.4856 224.971 227.638 2.317 0.2389

# hcov and non-hcov (CLsex) models equivalent, same density estimate:
derived(fitCLsex)
#       estimate SE.estimate       lcl      ucl       CVn       CVa       CVD
# esa 25.1768016          NA        NA       NA        NA        NA        NA
# D    0.7943821   0.2476404 0.4373251 1.442961 0.2238503 0.2169623 0.3117396

derived(fitCLh2)
#      estimate SE.estimate       lcl      ucl       CVn       CVa       CVD
# esa 17.679982          NA        NA       NA        NA        NA        NA
# D    1.131223   0.7363636 0.3528716 3.626433 0.2236068 0.6113339 0.6509448

derived(fithcov)
#       estimate SE.estimate       lcl      ucl       CVn       CVa       CVD
